For this VerseKit reads the top right corner of the game picture every few seconds, only while Star Citizen is in front. Without the display in the game nothing shows.

texte.s_ov_durch_h: The overlay stays visible but no longer catches clicks — in combat you shoot through it instead of at it. Moving it and its buttons stop working; you get back via the lock in the title bar, which stays clickable.

texte.s_ov_durch_auto_h: In first person and in flight the game hides the mouse pointer, but it keeps moving. While it is hidden, the overlay catches nothing — looking and shooting stay in the game. When the pointer is visible (mobiGlas, menus, desktop), the overlay works as usual. You do not need the lock for this.

texte.s_eigene_h:
Everything the tool knows about you lives here: blueprint inventory, watchlist, My Inventory, settings and exported files — in separate subfolders.

⭐ Playing Windows AND Linux on the same machine? Put this folder on a disk both systems can see, and set it to the same place in both. There is then only ONE inventory — nothing is synced, nothing can drift apart. Without it each system quietly keeps its own list, and you only notice when blueprints are missing.

The same goes for two machines: the same folder in the cloud or on a network drive.

When you switch, you are asked whether your data should come along. The previous folder is left untouched — nothing is deleted.

texte.s_dk_haldjas_idee: **Fade mode and click-through** — so an overlay helps in a fight instead of getting in the way. Plus the **farming list**: mark blueprints for farming straight from Crafting, armour and FPS weapons included — before, every route there went through a ship.
texte.s_dk_haldjas_bugs: Plus a dozen finds around the overlay, setup and updating — among them the collapsed overlay hanging off the screen edge in three corners out of four, the title bar that belongs at the bottom when the overlay sits in a bottom corner, the sluggish window build when opening the settings — and the green strip left behind in the old corner after a restart. Later also the raw key names in the setup wizard, and the renamed game folder that led to HOTFIX being recognised at all. And the blueprint list that stuttered when opening — it now comes up in a third of the time. His latest report brought two things at once: the sluggish program start, and the blueprints that no longer matched the catalogue with StarStrings. And the update that aborted at once because an old file could not be overwritten — since then the report also shows what an update attempt leaves behind. Plus the window that rebuilt itself completely when checking for an update, and hidden files that made settings get lost silently.
texte.s_dk_rurudotorg_idee: **Updates never arrived on Linux** — he kept at it long afterit looked like user error, until the cause was found.
texte.s_dk_rurudotorg_bugs: Plus the crash on the very first start, hard aborts that nevershowed up in the report — and a month of Discord Nitro for theserver.
texte.s_dk_greluc_idee: **Blueprints from your own account only** — his SC Extractor assigns every log to its account. VerseKit took over the idea: if you play two accounts on one computer, you no longer get the other one's blueprints.
texte.s_dk_greluc_idee2: **The "KRT (orange)" colour scheme** — colours and shapes follow the design system of his Profit Basetool.
texte.s_dk_greluc_bugs: **Review of the Basetool sync** — wait times after errors, a full stop after a block, only your own account's blueprints and more safely stored credentials on Linux. Plus the stock sync: materials and items land in the right store, materials with their quality. And a mass change the Basetool holds back is no longer resent on every sync, lots at a place outside the location catalog are no longer emptied, and unit storage only asks for the member list where you are a logistician.
texte.s_dk_greluc_bugs2: **A measured analysis of speed** — the overlay no longer stutters while you drag it and work runs in the background, and page switches no longer reread the settings every time.
texte.s_dk_parsul_idee: **Images in the bug report** — a screenshot now goes out right along with the report instead of being sent separately.
texte.s_dk_parsul_bugs: **The setup assistant wrote no blueprint details on a fresh install** — "the catalogue knows no missions", because the catalogue was only fetched after setup. Only visible when setting VerseKit up from scratch.
texte.s_dk_parsul_bugs2: **Nothing could be saved on his PC** — VerseKit had silently picked a Documents folder in OneDrive that Windows kept locked. Since then the setup asks where your data should live, and says so if nothing can be saved there.
texte.s_dk_parsul_bugs3: **The fuel nozzles were called "docking collars"** — that is only their internal type in the game.
texte.s_dk_parsul_bugs4: **Windows Defender took VerseKit for a trojan** — triggered by the refinery scanner's text recognition, which has been switched off since.
texte.s_dk_parsul_bugs5: **Windows reported a blocked access to the old folder on every start** — VerseKit kept trying to leave a pointer to the new data folder there. A locked folder is now left alone.
texte.s_dk_parsul_bugs6: **Error entries after closing the main window** — background work still reached into the window that was already being taken down.
texte.s_dk_parsul_bugs7: **The bug report left out where an error happened** — the error file he sent along showed it. The call sites are now part of the report.
texte.s_dk_choopa_idee: Developer of the **SC Launch Configurator** — he released his translations for use in this tool. Plus three nudges in one afternoon: **"Leave alone"** in the setup assistant (clicking on always did that, you just could not see it), the **blurry community mark** at higher scaling, and the toggle for **blueprints with no known source**. Later the advice to **count honestly** how many people really use VerseKit — which became the daily report without any ID.
texte.s_dk_yoshimitsu_idee: **Trade routes** — say where you are and what fits in your hold, and the tool works out what the next run is worth.
texte.s_dk_bushwick_idee: **From crafting straight to the blueprint** — and the button there now reads "Where from?" instead of being just a symbol. Plus **reputation points and cooldown in the mission text**: the figures were in the data but appeared nowhere in game.
texte.s_dk_bushwick_bugs: Plus a freshly received blueprint not showing up in the list right away, the mission log not refreshing the first time you opened it, and the ASOP terminal listing ships as `@vehicle_Name…` instead of their name — including when they came back after a patch. Also the update check that silently failed on some machines over a missing certificate. And the idea of a field for your message in the error report.
texte.s_dk_bushwick_idee2: **Reputation and cooldown in the contract texts** — asked twice, persistently, until they were not just there but actually noticeable.
texte.s_dk_bushwick_idee4: **Updating right after the game** — one minute after quitting instead of five.
texte.s_dk_bushwick_bugs2: The question of what a self-built **NDB-30** actually does better. Crafting only showed a factor per material, not the damage and DPS you end up with — now both are in a table.
texte.s_dk_bushwick_bugs3: And the **missing Hadanite** on the Attrition-5: ingredients the game hands out as single pieces — Hadanite, Dolivine, Sadaryx and eight more — were in no ingredient list at all. One find on one blueprint that sat in 255. And the `@…` placeholders in the game after a patch.
texte.s_dk_bushwick_idee3: **The way back after a page jump** — clicking an entry in the blueprint list takes you to crafting, and the only way back was the sidebar, which lost your search and your filter. Now there is a button that takes you back.
texte.s_dk_aeternitas_idee: **Progress for the watchlist only** — how far along you are with the blueprints you actually want. For that, finished ones now stay ticked off on the watchlist.
texte.s_dk_aeternitas_idee2: **Farming with locations** — what you need to farm and where it is, plus the places where you get several materials at once.
texte.s_dk_aeternitas_idee3: **Scan images for the signature scanner** — with his captures the scanner reads many more signatures out of the box.
texte.s_dk_p6_idee: **Scan images for the signature scanner** — with his captures the scanner reads many more signatures out of the box.
texte.s_dk_p6_bugs: **Ships doubled after a hangar import and the Basetool sync**, and an insurance that never reached the Basetool — his exact steps made both reproducible.
texte.s_dk_p6_bugs2: **Gems shown as "Plant"** in My Inventory once the Basetool syncs.
texte.s_dk_aeternitas_bugs: **Tooltips ran off the screen** when the overlay sits in the bottom right corner of the monitor. With the bar at the bottom they now always appear above the mouse pointer, not on the taskbar.
texte.s_dk_blackdog_idee2: **Update button in the title bar** — next to "What's new", and green with the version number as soon as a new version is out. One click installs it right away — after asking first, so a stray click in the middle of a game closes nothing.
texte.s_dk_blackdog_idee3: **Clear shader cache** — a button that empties the shader caches of Star Citizen and the graphics drivers when a patch brings graphics glitches or stutter.
texte.s_dk_blackdog_idee4: **Game settings in one place** — everything that writes into the game's files sits in its own group in the sidebar, plus a graphics page with the most important switches.
texte.s_dk_blackdog_idee: **What can be clicked should show it.** The note that you cannot tell which of the overlay icons actually do something — each one now lights up as the mouse passes over it. Everywhere in the program, not just in the overlay.
texte.s_dk_zwaersch_idee: **What is inside a wreck?** Wanting to know whether salvaging is worth it before you get out — that is where the whole ship-data connection came from, and with it „does this blueprint fit my ship". And the note that nobody can tell what the blueprint list actually searches — now the field says so. And the idea of looking up a bugged mission right on the **Issue Council** — that became the bug icon in the mission log.
texte.s_dk_zwaersch_bugs: That both import **and** export did not know the newer scmdb.net format, and that switching channels cost you your whole history — one single file brought all three to light. And that an empty search field never says what it can find — which turned into the hint text in **every** input field.
texte.s_dk_zwaersch_bugs2: That "I cannot see your entries in the game" can have two entirely different causes — nothing is written, or it is written to the language file the game does not load. The error report now names both side by side, and the case is readable in a single line. And that "Original" after StarStrings was not the original at all — the file stayed, foreign marks included. And that scmdb.net rejected the exported file, and the right button for it was nowhere to be found. And that the Issue Council search used old German titles as they were.
texte.s_dk_rurudotorg_bugs2: That the ship selection in “What's inside?” collapsed as soon as you grabbed the scrollbar — the mouse wheel worked, the scrollbar did not.
texte.s_dk_kynotnis_idee: **Reputation thresholds on ranks** — the reputation menu now shows how much reputation a rank starts at.
texte.s_dk_maluh_idee: **The fleet analysis in the hangar** — which gameplay loops your fleet covers, where the gaps are, which snubs have no mothership and what can be melted or upgraded via CCU. Idea and ship data come from his Fleetmanifest. Thank you!
texte.s_dk_drachennarr_idee: **Deaths and location from the game log** — the hint that a death can be told apart by your own body number and that the current place is in the log. Thank you!
texte.s_dk_drachennarr_bugs: **A review of the whole source code** — over thirty findings, among them feedback lost from background threads, user data that could be lost in a crash, and game files that could be left half-written. Plus the sluggish switch between card view and tab view, the SC Extractor blueprint file that could no longer be imported, the Basetool sign-in that failed on permissions not offered yet, and the blueprint list that froze on the "lost when ranking up" filter. Thank you!
texte.s_dk_rhino_idee: **Launch with MangoHud** — switching on the performance overlay on Linux straight from VerseKit. Thank you!
texte.s_dk_ryze_idee: **Recognising signatures automatically** — inspired by his mining sidecar. Thank you!
texte.s_dk_sotth_idee: **The Game.log check interval visible under “General”** — before, it was only reachable through the settings file.
texte.s_dk_fire_bugs: **The signature scanner never showed him anything** — and he sent his scanned images along with the report. The cause was in them: a single bright pixel split the opening of a zero in two, so a perfectly recognised digit counted as uncertain. Without his images this would not have been found. The same images later showed why **large HUD text** often stayed unreadable — even after teaching.
texte.s_dk_alyxone_idee: **Insurance in the JSON export** — he built the field into his Hangar Extension and shared his sample up front, so the import could read it from day one. And **the new app icon**: the concept and the original design are his, the current graphic implementation was made here. Thank you!
texte.s_dk_alyxone_bugs: **Clean ship names in the JSON export** — he split the names in his Hangar Extension into a short form and the Ship Matrix name, added the vehicles that come with a pledge, and let us know so the import could follow. Ships now arrive with clean names, special editions stay separate from the base ship, and extras like the G12 land in the hangar.
texte.s_dk_kynotnis_bugs: **Nothing started after a fresh install** — the setup wizard broke off right away. A fault nobody who was already set up could ever see: that one step only runs on the very first launch. And that the English installer showed two German lines — likewise only visible if you run it in English.
texte.s_dk_horthy_idee: **Your own resource stock** — enter it instead of doing themaths; crafting deducts the ingredients for you.
texte.s_dk_morkhan_idee: **Item details in game**, **launching Star Citizen from the tool**, since v3.4.0 the **selling tab**, having the **keyboard** on the joystick page too — and **back and forward** through visited pages, like in a browser.
texte.s_dk_morkhan_bugs: Plus more than twenty finds, among them 797 blueprints nobody ever got to see, a window that no longer fit the screen, and the withdrawn contract that came back after every start.

texte.s_bg_sig_kein_erz: No resource with this name has a signature.
texte.s_sg_lage_h: The small window with the scanned material stands directly above the signature in the game. Drag it in the picture to where it should stand; it then keeps the same distance to the signature. With the lock open you can also drag it in the game.
texte.s_sg_groesse_h: How large the letters and the window are, in per mille of the game window's height.
texte.s_sg_ort_h: Where the number and the ore stand while the info bar is on. Without the info bar the window always stands above the signature.
texte.s_sg_nachlauf_h: For this many seconds the display stays after the number has left the HUD.

texte.s_sx_hinweis: Every game log is read once and kept. The numbers stay even if Star Citizen or you delete the logs, and they move with your data folder. A death counts when the game creates your own body, a destroyed ship alone is not one. Injuries and jurisdictions are not reliably in the log, so they are not counted.

texte.s_sa_auto_h: Reads new logs by itself when VerseKit starts and when you open the statistics. Only what is new or has grown is read.
texte.s_nutzung_h: Once a day VerseKit reports its version, your system, language, which areas you use and which pages of the main window you open how often (and how many clicks it took to get there) and how often you use single storage functions — no ID, name or handle, no content or search terms. That way I can see how many people really use VerseKit, which parts, and what is hard to find. When switched off, nothing is counted at all. Every detail is listed in the privacy statement.
texte.s_scmdb_h: VerseKit reports new blueprints and running missions straight to scmdb.net: no export, no upload, no extra program. Sign in on scmdb.net, click "Watcher" at the top right and turn on "Enable Watcher"; the page has to be open for that. If your browser asks once whether scmdb.net may access apps on this device: allow it, let it remember, then reload the page. Everything goes into the scmdb account you are signed in with there, and only from LIVE and HOTFIX. If scmdb's own watcher is already running, use one or the other.

Weapons count per item and session; the share says how often a weapon showed up compared to the others in the same slot, not how long you carried it.

texte.s_dkv_haldjas_idee: Fade mode and click-through, so an overlay helps in a fight instead of getting in the way. Plus the farming list: mark blueprints for farming straight from Crafting, armour and FPS weapons included. Before, every route there went through a ship.
texte.s_dkv_haldjas_bugs: Plus a dozen finds around the overlay, setup and updating. Among them the collapsed overlay hanging off the screen edge in three corners out of four. The title bar that belongs at the bottom when the overlay sits in a bottom corner. The sluggish window build when opening the settings. And the green strip left behind in the old corner after a restart. Later also the raw key names in the setup wizard. And the renamed game folder that led to HOTFIX being recognised at all. And the blueprint list that stuttered when opening. It now opens in a third of the time. His latest report brought two things at once: the sluggish program start and the blueprints. Those blueprints no longer matched the catalogue with StarStrings. And the update that aborted at once because an old file could not be overwritten. Since then the report also shows what an update attempt leaves behind. Plus the window that rebuilt itself completely when checking for an update. Also hidden files that made settings get lost silently.
texte.s_dkv_rurudotorg_idee: Updates never arrived on Linux: He kept at it long after it looked like user error, until the cause was found.
texte.s_dkv_rurudotorg_bugs: Plus the crash on the very first start. Plus hard aborts that never showed up in the report. And a month of Discord Nitro for the server.
texte.s_dkv_rurudotorg_bugs2: That the ship selection in "What's inside?" collapsed as soon as you grabbed the scrollbar. The mouse wheel worked, the scrollbar did not.
texte.s_dkv_morkhan_idee: Item details in game, launching Star Citizen from the tool, and since v3.4.0 the selling tab. Plus having the keyboard on the joystick page too. And back and forward through visited pages, like in a browser.
texte.s_dkv_horthy_idee: Your own resource stock: enter it instead of doing the maths, and crafting deducts the ingredients for you.
texte.s_dkv_pinhead_idee: Mixing qualities: different amounts and qualities in one component, with the mixed quality.
texte.s_dkv_darthurmel_idee: The notes: a page of their own with as many notes as you like and a tile on the overview.
texte.s_dkv_smokyjohn_idee: The Contested Zones page: Executive Hangar timer, self timers for keycards and compboards, maps.
texte.s_dkv_lenoro_bugs: He measured at ARC-L1 with the same load and the same yield: Dinyx Solventation costs 446 aUEC and takes 4 hours 13 minutes, Pyrometric Chromalysis costs 2,676 aUEC and takes 42 minutes. The game texts say the opposite, so the advice of the Mining page was wrong. Both now follow his measurements.
texte.s_dkv_mindburnt_idee: The overlay opens on the events you choose: blueprint, scanner hit, contract, finished refinery job and catalogue entry. Each one can be switched on and off under Settings › Overlay.
texte.s_dkv_bushwick_idee: From crafting straight to the blueprint. The button there now reads "Where from?" instead of being just a symbol. Plus reputation points and cooldown in the mission text. The figures were in the data but appeared nowhere in game.
texte.s_dkv_bushwick_idee2: Reputation and cooldown in the contract texts: asked twice, persistently, until they were there and stood out.
texte.s_dkv_bushwick_idee3: The way back after a page jump: clicking an entry in the blueprint list opens crafting. The only way back was the sidebar, which lost your search and your filter. Now there is a button that takes you back.
texte.s_dkv_bushwick_idee4: Updating right after the game: one minute after quitting instead of five.
texte.s_dkv_bushwick_bugs: Plus a freshly received blueprint not showing up in the list right away. Also the mission log not refreshing the first time you opened it. And the ASOP terminal listing ships as `@vehicle_Name…` instead of their name. That included ships that came back after a patch. Then the update check that silently failed on some machines over a missing certificate. And the idea of a field for your message in the error report.
texte.s_dkv_bushwick_bugs2: The question of what a self-built NDB-30 actually does better. Crafting only showed a factor per material, not the damage and DPS you end up with. Now both are in a table.
texte.s_dkv_bushwick_bugs3: And the missing Hadanite on the Attrition-5. Ingredients the game hands out as single pieces were in no ingredient list at all. That covered Hadanite, Dolivine, Sadaryx and eight more. One find on one blueprint that sat in 255. And the `@…` placeholders in the game after a patch.
texte.s_dkv_choopa_idee: Developer of the SC Launch Configurator: He released his translations for use in this tool. Plus three nudges in one afternoon: "Leave alone" in the setup assistant. Clicking on always did that, you just could not see it. Then the blurry community mark at higher scaling. And the toggle for blueprints with no known source. Later the advice to count honestly how many people really use VerseKit. That became the daily report without any ID.
texte.s_dkv_yoshimitsu_idee: Trade routes: say where you are and what fits in your hold. The tool works out what the next run is worth.
texte.s_dkv_zwaersch_idee: What is inside a wreck? Wanting to know whether salvaging is worth it before you get out. That is where the whole ship-data connection came from, and with it "does this blueprint fit my ship". And the note that nobody can tell what the blueprint list actually searches: now the field says so. And the idea of looking up a bugged mission right on the Issue Council. That became the bug icon in the mission log.
texte.s_dkv_zwaersch_bugs: That both import and export did not know the newer scmdb.net format. And that switching channels cost you your whole history. One single file brought all three to light. And that an empty search field never says what it can find. That turned into the hint text in every input field.
texte.s_dkv_zwaersch_bugs2: That "I cannot see your entries in the game" can have two entirely different causes: nothing is written, or it is written to the language file the game does not load. The error report now names both side by side, and the case is readable in a single line. And that "Original" after StarStrings was not the original at all: the file stayed, foreign marks included. And that scmdb.net rejected the exported file, and the right button for it was nowhere to be found. And that the Issue Council search used old German titles as they were.
texte.s_dkv_aeternitas_idee: Progress for the watchlist only: how far along you are with the blueprints you actually want. For that, finished ones now stay ticked off on the watchlist.
texte.s_dkv_aeternitas_idee2: Farming with locations: what you need to farm and where it is. Plus the places where you get several materials at once.
texte.s_dkv_aeternitas_idee3: Scan images for the signature scanner: with his captures the scanner reads many more signatures out of the box.
texte.s_dkv_kynotnis_idee: Reputation thresholds on ranks: the reputation menu now shows how much reputation a rank starts at.
texte.s_dkv_kynotnis_bugs: Nothing started after a fresh install: The setup wizard broke off right away. A fault nobody who was already set up could ever see. That one step only runs on the very first launch. And that the English installer showed two German lines. That likewise only shows if you run it in English.
texte.s_dkv_maluh_idee: The fleet analysis in the hangar: which gameplay loops your fleet covers and where the gaps are. Plus which snubs have no mothership and what can be melted or upgraded via CCU. Idea and ship data come from his Fleetmanifest. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_drachennarr_idee: Deaths and location from the game log. The hint: a death can be told apart by your own body number. Plus the hint that the current place is in the log. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_drachennarr_bugs: A review of the whole source code: over thirty findings. Among them feedback lost from background threads. Also user data that could be lost in a crash. And game files that could be left half-written. Plus the sluggish switch between card view and tab view. Plus the SC Extractor blueprint file that could no longer be imported. Then the Basetool sign-in that failed on permissions not offered yet. And the blueprint list that froze on the "lost when ranking up" filter. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_rhino_idee: Launch with MangoHud: switching on the performance overlay on Linux straight from VerseKit. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_ryze_idee: Recognising signatures automatically, inspired by his mining sidecar. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_sotth_idee: The Game.log check interval visible under "General": before, it was only reachable through the settings file.
texte.s_dkv_fire_bugs: The signature scanner never showed him anything, and he sent his scanned images along with the report. The cause was in them: a single bright pixel split the opening of a zero in two. So a perfectly recognised digit counted as uncertain. Without his images this would not have been found. The same images later showed why large HUD text often stayed unreadable, even after teaching.
texte.s_dkv_shockwaffel_idee: The info bar above the game, with shard and scanner result. Plus the tip: the version number only in the main window. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_shockwaffel_bugs: After installing, the setup assistant lay hidden for him, and every further double-click ended without a word. Since then a second start brings the open window to the front. If VerseKit hangs, it tells you so. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_shockwaffel_idee2: The handle search with org members and history, the players on shard and server in the info bar, the size of overlay and bar and the larger game picture in the signature window. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_shockwaffel_bugs2: Blueprint notes that were missing on arms, helmets and lasers; since then they stand on nearly every item. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_george_bugs: Blueprints found with a code like [CIV-S2-A] in front of the name stood as “not in the catalogue”; since then VerseKit recognises them. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_kuehlwagen_idee2: The keys F13 to F24 for the hotkeys, the overlay snapping to the screen edge, a hotkey of its own for the handle search and hotkeys on a single key like F13. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_p6_idee3: The signature window while mining either above the signature or in the info bar, smaller with a slider and with a time to stay you set. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_lunaticsmile_idee: Craftable modules per ship: pick a ship, and crafting shows only parts that fit it, with the jump from the ship card in the hangar. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_sirfrog_bugs: A foreign text file loaded by hand stayed in the game folder; since then VerseKit replaces it and keeps it beside as a backup. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_shockwave_bugs: The mouse wheel over the Contested map zoomed instead of scrolling the page; since then it scrolls, and Ctrl zooms. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_kuehlwagen_bugs: The handle search hotkey stopped working after a mouse click into the game; since then it works without Esc too. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_rhino_bugs: On Linux the waiting overlay hung in the task bar as a dead window; since then it leaves the task bar, and without the game it shows again by default. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_fok_bugs: The overlay stayed in view without the game running and showed lines that only told its state; since then it waits hidden and shows just the eye. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_tomlov_idee: When many variants share one description in the game, the blueprint section now counts them instead of listing each one, so the quality below stays in view. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_greluc_idee: Blueprints from your own account only: His SC Extractor assigns every log to its account. VerseKit took over the idea: if you play two accounts on one computer, you no longer get the other one's blueprints.
texte.s_dkv_greluc_idee2: The "KRT (orange)" colour scheme: colours and shapes follow the design system of his Profit Basetool.
texte.s_dkv_greluc_bugs: Review of the Basetool sync: wait times after errors, a full stop after a block. Plus only your own account's blueprints and more safely stored credentials on Linux. Then the stock sync: materials and items land in the right store, materials with their quality. And a mass change the Basetool holds back is no longer resent on every sync. Lots at a place outside the location catalog are no longer emptied. And unit storage only asks for the member list where you are a logistician.
texte.s_dkv_greluc_bugs2: A measured analysis of speed: the overlay no longer stutters when you drag it. This holds while work runs in the background. Page switches no longer reread the settings every time. · The main window no longer opens larger than the screen.
texte.s_dkv_p6_idee: Scan images for the signature scanner: with his captures the scanner reads many more signatures out of the box.
texte.s_dkv_p6_idee2: More noticeable search lines: every search has a green border, a magnifier and a lighter background, so you find it at once.
texte.s_dkv_p6_bugs: Ships doubled after a hangar import and the Basetool sync, and an insurance that never reached the Basetool: His exact steps made both reproducible.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_idee: Images in the bug report: a screenshot now goes out right along with the report instead of being sent separately.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_bugs: The setup assistant wrote no blueprint details on a fresh install: "the catalogue knows no missions", because the catalogue was only fetched after setup. Only visible when setting VerseKit up from scratch.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_bugs2: Nothing could be saved on his PC. VerseKit had silently picked a Documents folder in OneDrive that Windows kept locked. Since then the setup asks where your data should live. It also says so if nothing can be saved there.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_bugs3: The fuel nozzles were called "docking collars": that is only their internal type in the game.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_bugs4: Windows Defender took VerseKit for a trojan: triggered by the refinery scanner's text recognition, which has been switched off since.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_bugs5: Windows reported a blocked access to the old folder on every start: VerseKit kept trying to leave a pointer to the new data folder there. A locked folder is now left alone.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_bugs6: Error entries after closing the main window: background work still reached into the window that was already being taken down.
texte.s_dkv_parsul_bugs7: The bug report left out where an error happened: the error file he sent along showed it. The call sites are now part of the report.
texte.s_dkv_blackdog_idee: What can be clicked should show it. The note that you cannot tell which of the overlay icons actually do something. Each one now lights up as the mouse passes over it. It applies everywhere in the program, also outside the overlay.
texte.s_dkv_blackdog_idee2: Update button in the title bar, next to "What's new". It turns green and shows the version number as soon as a new version is out. One click installs it right away, after asking first. That way a stray click in the middle of a game closes nothing.
texte.s_dkv_blackdog_idee3: Clear shader cache: a button that empties the shader caches of Star Citizen and the graphics drivers. It helps when a patch brings graphics glitches or stutter.
texte.s_dkv_blackdog_idee4: Game settings in one place: everything that writes into game files has its own sidebar group. Plus a graphics page with the most important switches.
texte.s_dkv_blackdog_idee5: Anti-AFK: an overlay button that, on Windows, presses Alt + X every five minutes. It does so while the game is in front and nothing else is pressed. Off by default.
texte.s_dkv_alyxone_idee: Insurance in the JSON export: He built the field into his Hangar Extension. He shared his sample up front, so the import could read it from day one. And the new app icon: the concept and the original design are his. The current graphic implementation was made here. Thank you!
texte.s_dkv_alyxone_bugs: Clean ship names in the JSON export: He split the names in his Hangar Extension. The names are now split into a short form and the Ship Matrix name. He added the vehicles that come with a pledge. And he let us know, so the import could follow. Ships now arrive with clean names. Special editions stay separate from the base ship. Extras like the G12 land in the hangar.
texte.s_dkv_katschaeng_idee: Shopping basket for 5.0: put parts from the shops into the shopping list with a quantity, see the cost and every place to buy each part at a glance, work through the route with a tick per stop, keep sets like “FPS set heavy” as a template, and go back from a part to the results without losing the search and the filters. Thank you!

texte.s_p3_verschluesselt: The game data of this channel are encrypted. VerseKit does not read them and keeps the last state it read.

texte.s_sle_buchen_aus: You are a logistician here. Booking can be switched on under Settings › Connection & sync.
texte.s_sle_kein_logistiker: Booking is on, but the Basetool does not list you as a logistician in this unit. That takes the logistician flag or a leadership rank directly in this unit. Until then, share your own items in the Basetool in your browser.
texte.s_sle_mitglied: Logisticians book into the unit storage. You share your own items in the Basetool in your browser and stay their owner. If you are a logistician, switch on "Book as a logistician" under Settings › Connection & sync.
texte.s_sle_masse: Please confirm in the browser. Only then is it booked.
texte.s_sle_noch_dran: One moment, the previous request is still running.
texte.s_sle_r_ambiguous: Refused: the name fits several goods. Please be more precise.
texte.s_sle_r_version_conflict: Refused: the entry has changed meanwhile. The new state is fetched, please try again.
texte.s_sle_ware_geaendert: The form changed while the goods were looked up. Nothing was booked. Please click "Book in" again.
texte.s_sle_ware_mehrdeutig: "{0}" is not unique at the Basetool. Nothing was booked. Pick the right goods below.
texte.s_sle_ware_stueck: "{0}" is counted in pieces. Choose pieces under "Counted in". Nothing was booked.
texte.s_sle_ware_unbekannt: The Basetool does not know "{0}". Nothing was booked. Pick goods from the list.
texte.s_sle_ziel_fehlt: Pick the unit it should go to.
texte.s_sle_keine_zieleinheit: Right now there is no other unit you may book in. Move it to a location or a member.
texte.s_sle_eintrag_weg: The entry is gone meanwhile. The form is closed.
texte.s_sle_beispiel: Sample data: the preview shows a made-up Basetool. What you book stays in this window.
texte.s_sle_beispiel_browser: The preview opens no browser here.
texte.s_sle_holen_fehler: The storage could not be fetched: {0}
texte.s_btv_lead: Syncs blueprints, storage and hangar with the KRT Profit Basetool, both ways. Only what you connect and turn on gets synced.
texte.s_btv_name_h: This is the name of this computer under "Connected applications" in the Basetool. It lets you tell Windows and Linux apart and disconnect them one by one. It is not your handle.
texte.s_btv_name_falsch: Allowed: letters, digits, spaces and - _ . (40 characters at most)
texte.s_btv_code_h: Open the address in your browser, sign in to the Basetool and type this code:
texte.s_btv_code_oben: A code is now shown above. Open the address, sign in to the Basetool and type it in. VerseKit then syncs on its own.
texte.s_btv_erst_bereich: First turn on below what you want to sync. Then "Connect" appears here. That way one sign-in covers everything.
texte.s_btv_code_warnung: Only ever type the code yourself. If someone sends you a code to confirm, it is a scam: it would give them access to your Basetool.
texte.s_btv_abgelehnt: The Basetool declined the connection. Click "Connect" again.
texte.s_btv_abgelaufen: The code has expired (10 minutes). Click "Connect" again.
texte.s_btv_sandbox: Test environment: this does not connect to the real Basetool.
texte.s_btv_testbetrieb: Test mode: VerseKit does not write to the Basetool and does not sync.
texte.s_btv_f_schreibwache: Check mode: this change was held back and not sent to the Basetool.
texte.s_btv_override: Developer settings for the Basetool are set but have no effect without SC_BP_BASETOOL_ISSUER. You connect to the real Basetool.
texte.s_btv_datei: Your system has no keyring (Secret Service). So the credentials are kept in a file only you can read: {ordner}
texte.s_btv_bauplaene_h: Syncs your blueprints with the Basetool.
texte.s_btv_rechte_fehlen: VerseKit needs one more permission for this area. For that you sign in again. The connection stays the same.
texte.s_btv_nicht_angeboten: The Basetool does not offer this permission yet. When it does, the button for it appears here.
texte.s_btv_stand_bp: Last sync: {gesendet} sent, {uebernommen} taken over, {entfernt} removed.
texte.s_btv_ueberblick: In the Basetool: {n} blueprints, {m} of them linked to your collection
texte.s_btv_unbekannt: The Basetool does not know {n} blueprints under any name. They stay here only.
texte.s_btv_lager_h: Syncs "My Inventory" with your stock in the Basetool.
texte.s_btv_lager_ueberblick: In the Basetool: {n} lots in your stock
texte.s_btv_lager_stand: Last sync: {gesendet} lots sent, {uebernommen} taken over.
texte.s_btv_lager_umgezogen: {n} lots were in the wrong store and moved: materials to "For crafting", items to "Items". Nothing was booked in the Basetool for this.
texte.s_btv_lager_ort: {n} lots stay here because the Basetool does not list the place as a storage location: {orte}
texte.s_btv_lager_material: {n} lots stay here because the Basetool does not know the material.
texte.s_btv_lager_geschuetzt: {n} lots in the Basetool stay unchanged because VerseKit skips their place.
texte.s_btv_lager_angebote: Note: this reduced or removed {n} offers on the Basetool material exchange.
texte.s_btv_hangar_h: Syncs your ships with your hangar in the Basetool.
texte.s_btv_hangar_ueberblick: In the Basetool: {n} ships, {m} linked to your hangar
texte.s_btv_hangar_stand: Last sync: {verknuepft} linked, {angelegt} created, {uebernommen} taken over.
texte.s_btv_hangar_unbekannt: The Basetool does not know {n} ship types. They stay here only.
texte.s_btv_hangar_missionen: Note: {n} missions in the Basetool lost a ship through this.
texte.s_btv_einheit_uebernommen: VerseKit took over the unit changed in the Basetool: {n} ships.
texte.s_btv_einheit_abgelehnt: The Basetool did not accept the unit, its own applies: {n} ships.
texte.s_btv_einheit_recht: The unit choice in the hangar needs a permission. The sync works without it too.
texte.s_btv_einheit_recht_lager: You cannot yet put anything from "My Inventory" into a unit's storage. That needs a permission for the list of your units. The sync works without it too.
texte.s_btv_einheit_neu_h: Applies only when VerseKit creates a ship in the Basetool. On the ship card in the hangar you change the unit per ship. If someone changes it in the Basetool, that one applies.
texte.s_btv_bedarf_h: Shows what your unit's open orders still need.
texte.s_btv_bedarf_kein_recht: Only members of a unit taking part in the profit sharing see the demand. The Basetool does not release it for your account.
texte.s_btv_rechte_zusatz: The extra features of this area need a permission. The area works without it too.
texte.s_btv_staffellager_logistiker: Units where you are a logistician: {n}
texte.s_btv_staffellager_buchen_h: Book in, book out, sell, move, notes, stolen marker and reservations. This works only in units where you are a logistician. Every booking appears in the Basetool under your name and can be undone there.
texte.s_btv_konflikte_h: You removed these blueprints in the Basetool, but your game logs show them. VerseKit does not send them back on its own.
texte.s_btv_wieder_hoch: Put them back into the Basetool anyway
texte.s_btv_hier_entfernt_h: You removed these blueprints in VerseKit. They are still in the Basetool.
texte.s_btv_auch_dort: Remove them in the Basetool too
texte.s_btv_vorgemerkt: Noted. The sync takes care of it in a moment.
texte.s_btv_lager_konflikte_h: These lots have different amounts here and in the Basetool. Which one applies?
texte.s_btv_hangar_weg_h: These ships are missing here but still in the Basetool. This happens, for example, after a pledge import without them.
texte.s_btv_hangar_dort_weg_h: You removed these ships in the Basetool. They are still here. VerseKit does not create them again on its own.
texte.s_btv_masse_h: This time a lot would change in the Basetool at once. The Basetool holds the change back for 30 minutes until you confirm it there. Until then VerseKit does not send this area again.
texte.s_btv_gesperrt: A change is waiting for your confirmation in the Basetool. Confirm it there.
texte.s_btv_gesperrt_alt: The confirmation in the Basetool has expired. The change did not go through. "Sync now" sends it again.
texte.s_btv_datenschutz: VerseKit sends only to the Basetool. It sends only what you connected and turned on. That covers blueprints and stock lots with material, place, quality and amount. For ships, VerseKit sends type, insurance, own name, ready and unit. It never sends price or package. For the account check, your RSI handle is added. Your credentials stay on this computer. They never appear in your VerseKit data, a backup or an error report.
